included: DeerFlow 2.0 browser, gateway, runtime, model, tool, skill, sandbox, persistence, streaming, and artifact boundaries
Current DeepResearchForecast Stage-1 API-to-orchestrator-to-embedded-DeerFlow-2 bridge, including the default single shared Track-B actor-intelligence path and its artifact handoff
Implemented/configured drf2 target interfaces, explicitly marked pre-cutover
excluded: Detailed downstream simulation/report internals outside the DeerFlow 2 integration boundary
scope.interpretation: The 68 interfaces below are mapped from the current working tree atop source_revision. Each entry is a typed boundary, not necessarily a network API. passes_and_receptions records who sends, who receives, and what crosses. Authority describes which side is canonical for that datum; durability describes what survives process restart.

status_legend.native_available: Implemented in public DeerFlow 2.0 and cross-checked against the optional local source drop; enabled/disabled by deployment policy. The clean-clone fallback pin is an older DeerFlow 2 revision.
status_legend.active_current: Part of the current authoritative DeepAgentForecast Stage-1 path.
status_legend.conditional_current: Part of the current path only when a flag, mode, data condition, retry, or failure path is active.
status_legend.pre_cutover: Implemented/configured in drf2 but not yet authoritative for production runs.
status_legend.opaque_external: The repository sees only the outer request/response contract.

interfaces.input: Typed user text plus selected model, thinking flag, enabled subagents, attachments/resources, and thread/runtime options.
interfaces.transport: Frontend state -> JSON request and streaming client hook.
interfaces.receiver: Gateway thread/run endpoints.
interfaces.output: A new or existing thread identifier, run identifier, and live event subscription.
interfaces.authority: The submitted user message is authoritative user input; the gateway validates and normalizes the run envelope.
interfaces.durability: The browser form is transient. Accepted messages become thread checkpoint/run state.
interfaces.security_boundary: Browser-originated content is untrusted and crosses HTTP, CSRF/auth, context allowlisting, upload/resource validation, and tool/sandbox policy boundaries.

passes_and_receptions.payload: thread/run JSON plus credentials and stream controls

interfaces.notes: The UI is one client. The Runs API and embedded client can submit equivalent turns without the browser.

interfaces.input: One or more files within configured per-file size, aggregate size, count, filename, and path limits. A suffix is consulted only when optional document conversion is configured; there is no general upload extension allowlist in this path.
interfaces.transport: Multipart HTTP upload.
interfaces.receiver: Gateway upload router, then thread/user workspace and optional sandbox synchronization.
interfaces.output: Validated stored file metadata/path that can be referenced from run context or read by tools.
interfaces.authority: Stored workspace bytes are authoritative after successful validation/write; client filenames are labels, not trusted paths.
interfaces.durability: Files persist on the configured workspace/storage backend until removed by lifecycle policy.
interfaces.security_boundary: Filename/path normalization, per-file/aggregate size and count limits, user/thread workspace scope, and sandbox path mapping. Optional conversion can be suffix-specific, but unsupported extensions are not rejected by a general allowlist here.
interfaces.notes: Document conversion is deployment-configurable and is not intrinsically an LLM call.

interfaces.input: Browser/API request paths, headers, cookies, bodies, and optional streaming connection.
interfaces.transport: Nginx HTTP reverse proxy with path routing/rewrite and buffering controls.
interfaces.receiver: Frontend server or gateway API.
interfaces.output: Proxied HTTP response or SSE stream.
interfaces.authority: Nginx owns external path routing; application services own request semantics.
interfaces.durability: None at the proxy layer.
interfaces.security_boundary: First deployed network boundary; preserves/sets forwarding headers and applies response/stream settings. Application auth remains downstream.
interfaces.notes: SSE paths require response buffering to remain disabled end to end.

interfaces.producer: Browser/API client and gateway authentication dependencies
interfaces.input: Credentials/cookies, CSRF token/header for browser mutations, and requested user/thread identity.
interfaces.transport: HTTP headers/cookies and gateway dependency injection.
interfaces.receiver: Thread, run, upload, artifact, suggestion, and tool-context services.
interfaces.output: Authenticated user context or rejected request.
interfaces.authority: Gateway-authenticated identity is authoritative; arbitrary client context fields do not override it.
interfaces.durability: Authentication state depends on deployment; resolved request context is transient per request.
interfaces.security_boundary: Separates user-controlled request metadata from trusted runtime identity and ownership checks.
interfaces.notes: Exact authentication backend is deployment-configurable; ownership validation remains a service boundary.

interfaces.input: Optional client-selected thread_id plus thread metadata.
interfaces.transport: POST /api/threads and related thread APIs.
interfaces.receiver: Gateway thread service/store.
interfaces.output: Created or idempotently resolved thread record.
interfaces.authority: Thread store is canonical for ownership and metadata; checkpoint store is canonical for graph state.
interfaces.durability: Thread metadata survives restart only when the configured thread store is durable; an in-memory configuration is process-local.
interfaces.security_boundary: Path thread IDs are ownership-scoped and later path-based run/artifact operations validate that owner. The run-config seam described below can nevertheless choose a different effective checkpoint namespace during execution.
interfaces.notes: drf2's driver relies on the create operation being idempotent for one persistent path thread. That record does not by itself prove that every later run executes in the same effective checkpoint namespace.

interfaces.producer: Browser stream hook, SDK, or Runs API client
interfaces.input: Path thread ID plus RunCreate fields: assistant_id, input, command, metadata, broadly forwarded RunnableConfig overrides in config, allowlisted DeerFlow-specific overrides in context, webhook, checkpoint_id/checkpoint, interrupt_before/after, stream_mode/subgraphs/resumable, on_disconnect/on_completion, multitask_strategy, after_seconds, if_not_exists, and feedback_keys. The current service consumes only a subset of the declared lifecycle fields.
interfaces.transport: POST /api/threads/{thread_id}/runs or /runs/stream.
interfaces.receiver: Gateway run service and RunManager.
interfaces.output: RunRecord immediately, and optionally an SSE stream joined to its events.
interfaces.authority: RunManager/store owns lifecycle status; graph/checkpointer owns agent state. The route authenticates and looks up the path thread, but a client-supplied body.config.configurable.thread_id can currently select a different execution/checkpoint namespace.
interfaces.durability: Run records/events persist according to configured stores; live task handles are process-local.
interfaces.security_boundary: The path thread is ownership-checked and authenticated user_id is server-stamped. body.context uses a DeerFlow-key allowlist, but body.config is broadly forwarded: configurable.thread_id can override the path thread in the no-context branch and top-level values can override defaults such as recursion_limit. This is a current trust seam, not an owner-bound invariant.

passes_and_receptions.payload: path-owner-checked run specification plus broadly forwarded config overrides

interfaces.notes: Background runs and stream-joined runs share the same run lifecycle, but disconnect policy differs. POST /runs/wait is a distinct create-and-wait route itemized next. webhook, checkpoint_id, inline checkpoint, stream_resumable, on_completion, after_seconds, if_not_exists, and feedback_keys are schema-declared but not consumed by the current start_run path. Schema-valid multitask_strategy=enqueue is rejected as HTTP 501. The config/thread namespace seam should be closed before treating gateway isolation as strict.

interfaces.input: Path thread ID plus the same RunCreate body used by ordinary run creation.
interfaces.transport: POST /api/threads/{thread_id}/runs/wait.
interfaces.receiver: start_run schedules the worker; wait_for_run_completion observes its terminal record; the route then performs a checkpointer lookup keyed by the path thread ID.
interfaces.output: Final path-thread channel values when a checkpoint exists, otherwise a terminal status/error projection.
interfaces.authority: The created graph executes under the effective merged RunnableConfig, but the final response lookup reconstructs state from the path thread. A client-supplied configurable.thread_id override can therefore checkpoint namespace B while the wait response reads namespace A.
interfaces.durability: Run/state durability depends on the configured run store and checkpointer; the blocking HTTP wait itself is transient.
interfaces.security_boundary: The path thread is ownership-checked, but the broad body.config seam can select another execution/checkpoint namespace while the response remains path-keyed.

passes_and_receptions.payload: new run under effective merged config
final channel values or status/error fallback

interfaces.notes: This is create-and-wait, not a wait endpoint for an existing run. Its split effective-config/path-thread authority makes the configurable.thread_id seam externally observable.

interfaces.input: New run plus existing active run state and requested multitask strategy.
interfaces.transport: In-process RunManager coordination backed by run store state.
interfaces.receiver: Existing run and/or newly scheduled worker.
interfaces.output: Accepted; rejected/conflict; or the prior run interrupted/rolled back before admission. Only reject, interrupt, and rollback are implemented; enqueue is schema-valid but returns HTTP 501.
interfaces.authority: The process-local RunManager serializes admission by path thread ID; it is not a distributed or effective-checkpoint-namespace lock.
interfaces.durability: Admission locks and task-cancellation handles are process-local. Run statuses survive restart only when the configured run store is durable; MemoryRunStore does not.
interfaces.security_boundary: It prevents overlapping runs admitted under the same path thread in one manager process. Because body.config can override configurable.thread_id, distinct path threads can still alias one effective checkpoint namespace.
interfaces.notes: drf2's deterministic Runs API client uses multitask_strategy=reject to preserve intended single-writer behavior on its one path thread. That is not a strict global checkpoint-namespace invariant until the config/thread override seam is closed. There is no implemented queue/replacement behavior in this source snapshot.

interfaces.input: Normalized input/command; authenticated user_id; path-derived run identity; and merged client/server RunnableConfig containing model/thinking/subagent configuration, resources, sandbox/workspace, recursion and stream settings. Client body.config is not comprehensively allowlisted.
interfaces.transport: In-process worker constructs RunnableConfig and RuntimeContext, then calls graph.astream.
interfaces.receiver: Compiled lead-agent LangGraph.
interfaces.output: Graph state transitions and namespaced stream events.
interfaces.authority: Authenticated user_id is server-stamped and body.context is selectively merged, but config.configurable.thread_id and arbitrary top-level RunnableConfig values can survive into the worker. The effective config/checkpoint namespace, not merely the path thread, governs graph execution.
interfaces.durability: Runtime objects are transient; accepted state transitions are checkpointed.
interfaces.security_boundary: This is the main control/data-plane join. Authenticated identity and allowlisted body.context fields are bounded, but broad body.config forwarding leaves a current thread-namespace and runtime-option trust seam before tools, model factories, sandbox, memory, and subagents.

passes_and_receptions.payload: input/command plus server-stamped identity and merged, partly client-controlled runtime config

interfaces.notes: Embedded DeerFlowClient builds an equivalent graph/runtime boundary in-process without gateway HTTP.

interfaces.input: Current AgentState, runtime context, model request, tool calls, and tool results.
interfaces.transport: Ordered LangChain/LangGraph AgentMiddleware hooks around model and tool execution.
interfaces.receiver: Subsequent middleware, model node, tool node, and final graph state.
interfaces.output: Injected/trimmed/summarized messages, selected model/tools, normalized errors, title/memory updates, loop/safety decisions, and budgeted tool messages.
interfaces.authority: Middleware order is authoritative for how state and tool/model requests are transformed.
interfaces.durability: Only resulting state updates are checkpointed; middleware objects/caches are generally process-local.
interfaces.security_boundary: Enforces tool policy, sandbox/tool-result bounds, safety finish reasons, loop detection, and runtime-owned identity around untrusted model actions.
interfaces.notes: Summarization, title, memory, and subagent model calls are itemized in the call inventory.

interfaces.input: Normalized messages, system instructions, bound tool schemas, max tokens, thinking/reasoning configuration, sampling parameters, credentials, and timeout/retry settings.
interfaces.transport: Provider SDK or direct HTTP. The inspected native providers do not invoke a local CLI subprocess for inference.
interfaces.receiver: Configured model provider.
interfaces.output: AIMessage content/reasoning/tool_calls, usage, finish reason, response metadata, or typed error.
interfaces.authority: Provider response is authoritative only as model output; tool calls remain proposals subject to harness policy and validation.
interfaces.durability: Response enters checkpoint/run events according to graph/store policy; provider-side retention is external.
interfaces.security_boundary: Credentials and selected context leave the local runtime. Provider configuration and tool-schema exposure bound what is sent.
interfaces.notes: Claude can source OAuth credentials from Claude CLI-origin auth but invokes the Anthropic SDK. The Codex provider can read Codex CLI-origin credentials but calls the Codex Responses endpoint directly over HTTP. Credential provenance is not inference transport. Logical call families and retry multiplicity are enumerated separately in deerflow2-call-inventory.json.

interfaces.producer: Harness config loader and tool builder
interfaces.input: Configured builtin/config-reflected tools, tool groups, MCP/ACP extensions, runtime sandbox capabilities, model capabilities, and enabled feature flags.
interfaces.transport: In-process reflection/import plus extension discovery.
interfaces.receiver: Lead-agent/subagent tool binding and deferred tool catalog.
interfaces.output: Deduplicated named tools with schemas, descriptions, groups, and execution callables.
interfaces.authority: Configured/local tool registry and extension discovery are authoritative; name precedence/deduplication determines collisions.
interfaces.durability: Registry is built per agent/runtime and cached as implementation permits; configuration files are durable.
interfaces.security_boundary: Bash, vision, sandbox, user, and policy gates can omit tools even if configured.
interfaces.notes: A configured tool is not necessarily exposed to every agent or every turn.

interfaces.input: Text query over a policy-filtered catalog of deferred tool names/descriptions/schemas.
interfaces.transport: Local tool invocation and catalog search/hash matching.
interfaces.receiver: DeferredToolManager/catalog.
interfaces.output: Matching tool metadata and promotion of selected tools into subsequent model requests.
interfaces.authority: The policy-filtered catalog is authoritative; tool_search cannot promote a tool excluded by allowed-tool policy.
interfaces.durability: Catalog and promotions are runtime/thread state, not external durable artifacts unless reflected in checkpoint messages.
interfaces.security_boundary: Prevents the model from discovering/promoting tools outside the current agent/skill policy.
interfaces.notes: Current Stage-1 config disables tool_search; drf2 pre-cutover enables it for the larger KG/simulation catalog.

interfaces.input: Tool name, call ID, and JSON arguments proposed by the model.
interfaces.transport: LangGraph tool node through validation, policy, middleware, and the tool callable.
interfaces.receiver: Builtin/config-reflected/MCP/ACP/sandbox tool.
interfaces.output: ToolMessage containing text/structured/multimodal result or a normalized error.
interfaces.authority: Tool implementation owns observed result; the model does not execute actions directly.
interfaces.durability: ToolMessage joins checkpoint state. Side effects/files persist only according to tool/backend semantics.
interfaces.security_boundary: Tool name/schema validation, allowed-tool policy, runtime identity, sandbox/path checks, error handling, and output budget all interpose.

passes_and_receptions.payload: validated arguments plus trusted runtime context

interfaces.notes: The next model invocation receives the ToolMessage, producing the iterative agent loop.

interfaces.input: Enabled MCP server definitions, transport settings, command/URL, environment, auth, and runtime user/thread scoping.
interfaces.transport: MCP stdio or HTTP/session transport.
interfaces.receiver: Configured MCP server.
interfaces.output: Remote tool list/schemas wrapped as DeerFlow-compatible tools.
interfaces.authority: The MCP server advertises its tools; local config and policy decide whether each is enabled/exposed.
interfaces.durability: Server configuration is durable; discovered wrappers/session pools are runtime state.
interfaces.security_boundary: Launching a stdio server crosses a process/env boundary; HTTP crosses a network/auth boundary. Tool policy still filters advertised capabilities.
interfaces.notes: Discovery does not itself imply a tool will be exposed or called.

interfaces.input: Validated tool name/arguments plus runtime user/thread/sandbox-derived cwd and configured environment.
interfaces.transport: Pooled MCP stdio session per scoped runtime or MCP HTTP transport.
interfaces.receiver: MCP server tool implementation.
interfaces.output: MCP text, image, embedded-resource, resource-link, structured content, or error blocks converted for LangChain/DeerFlow. Audio and unknown block types have no dedicated converter and fall through to textual string representation.
interfaces.authority: MCP server owns operation result; local converter owns the shape presented to the agent.
interfaces.durability: Tool result enters checkpoint; server-side mutations and files follow server semantics; sessions are pooled runtime resources.
interfaces.security_boundary: Arguments leave the harness process. User/thread pooling keys, cwd/temp roots, environment, auth, timeouts, and content conversion bound the call.

passes_and_receptions.payload: tool name, arguments, trusted runtime scope

interfaces.notes: Any model calls internal to an MCP server are opaque and separately marked in the call inventory.

interfaces.input: Tool-requested sandbox path and operation-specific arguments/content.
interfaces.transport: Sandbox provider API with virtual-to-host/container path mapping.
interfaces.receiver: Thread/user sandbox filesystem.
interfaces.output: Bounded listing/content/search/edit result or validation error.
interfaces.authority: Sandbox provider's normalized path mapping is authoritative; raw model-proposed paths are not.
interfaces.durability: Workspace writes persist according to sandbox provider; reads/results in ToolMessages are checkpointed.
interfaces.security_boundary: Path normalization, allowed roots, traversal prevention, symlink/file checks, operation/tool policy, and output limits.
interfaces.notes: Current Stage-1 and drf2 use a local sandbox provider; deployment providers can change the isolation boundary.

interfaces.input: Model-proposed shell command and sandbox/runtime working context.
interfaces.transport: Sandbox provider command execution or explicitly allowed host bash.
interfaces.receiver: Shell process.
interfaces.output: Exit status and bounded stdout/stderr.
interfaces.authority: Sandbox/config policy decides whether execution is permitted and where it runs.
interfaces.durability: Process is transient; filesystem/network side effects follow command/provider semantics; result enters checkpoint.
interfaces.security_boundary: High-risk boundary controlled by tool exposure, allow_host_bash, sandbox provider, user identity, cwd/path limits, timeouts, and output caps.
interfaces.notes: Both repository configs allow host bash only under their stated trusted local single-user assumption.

interfaces.input: Potentially large text/multimodal result or thrown error.
interfaces.transport: ToolErrorHandlingMiddleware and ToolOutputBudgetMiddleware.
interfaces.receiver: Agent graph/model and optional .tool-results workspace storage.
interfaces.output: Normalized ToolMessage; large output can become head/tail preview plus pointer to the externalized full result.
interfaces.authority: Full externalized bytes are authoritative when created; preview is explicitly partial. Error messages are normalized observations, not successful results.
interfaces.durability: Externalized files persist in the workspace; ToolMessages persist in checkpoint state.
interfaces.security_boundary: Caps context amplification and prevents raw exceptions from crashing ordinary recoverable tool loops; exempt tools remain configurable.

passes_and_receptions.payload: full result if externalization threshold is crossed

interfaces.notes: drf2 enables externalization at 12000 characters under .tool-results.

interfaces.input: Enabled public/custom skill metadata, SKILL.md body, optional resources, available-skill whitelist, and slash activation syntax.
interfaces.transport: Local skill storage scan followed by SkillActivationMiddleware message injection.
interfaces.receiver: Lead/subagent model request and tool policy union.
interfaces.output: Selected skill instructions inserted into agent context, with safe/full content controls and recent-skill preservation metadata.
interfaces.authority: On-disk enabled skill body is authoritative for workflow instructions; the available-skill whitelist bounds visibility.
interfaces.durability: Skills persist on disk; injected skill messages become checkpoint state and may be preserved across summarization.
interfaces.security_boundary: Skill enablement, whitelist, safe-content mode, security scan/evolution policy, and allowed-tools constrain instruction/code injection.
interfaces.notes: Current Stage-1 whitelists exactly deep-research, actor-ontology-research, prediction-markets, and forecast-visuals.

interfaces.input: Agent base tools, per-agent whitelist, active skills' allowed-tools, deferred catalog, and feature/runtime capability gates.
interfaces.transport: In-process policy computation before model tool binding/promotion.
interfaces.receiver: Lead/subagent model request and tool_search catalog.
interfaces.output: Final allowed tool-name set and filtered tool objects.
interfaces.authority: Computed policy is authoritative for exposure; model text cannot grant itself additional tools.
interfaces.durability: Policy is recomputed/runtime state; active-skill messages are checkpointed.
interfaces.security_boundary: Least-capability boundary between untrusted model intent and executable tools.
interfaces.notes: Policy applies both to immediately bound tools and deferred discovery.

interfaces.input: Named subagent/task description, custom prompt, allowed skills/tools, model/turn/timeout settings, and inherited sandbox/user/thread context.
interfaces.transport: In-process task tool and ephemeral compiled subagent graph.
interfaces.receiver: Subagent executor/model/tool loop.
interfaces.output: Terminal subagent text, message/usage/status metadata, or structured task error returned as a ToolMessage.
interfaces.authority: Parent owns final decisions; subagent output is evidence/advice until the parent receives and acts on it.
interfaces.durability: Subagent checkpointer=false. Parent ToolMessage and any shared-workspace files persist.
interfaces.security_boundary: Per-subagent model/tool/skill whitelist, task timeout/max_turns, concurrency cap, and inherited trusted runtime context.
interfaces.notes: Current Stage-1 gates this boundary with --subagents; drf2 defines four pre-cutover custom agents.

interfaces.input: Tool-call arguments containing a question, optional context/options, and clarification type.
interfaces.transport: Middleware creates a ToolMessage and returns Command(goto=END); the client displays that terminal turn and submits any answer as a new HumanMessage in a later run.
interfaces.receiver: Checkpointed message state and frontend/API client; a later ordinary turn receives the user's answer.
interfaces.output: Formatted clarification ToolMessage followed by normal run completion, not a LangGraph interrupt payload or Command.resume value.
interfaces.authority: The persisted ToolMessage records the question; the user's later HumanMessage is authoritative for the answer.
interfaces.durability: The clarification ToolMessage is checkpointed with the completed turn. There is no paused clarification frame to resume.
interfaces.security_boundary: The next turn follows ordinary thread/run access controls and tool policy; clarification itself grants no capability.
interfaces.notes: Despite comments that use the word interrupt, this implementation terminates the turn at END and does not call LangGraph interrupt().

interfaces.producer: LangGraph node interrupt or configured interrupt_before/interrupt_after boundary
interfaces.input: Interrupt payload and checkpointed graph/task state.
interfaces.transport: Interrupt/checkpoint content appears in graph value/update events; a later run can submit command.resume.
interfaces.receiver: Client/operator and later worker invocation of the checkpointed graph.
interfaces.output: Resumed graph transitions, explicit cancellation, or a still-paused checkpoint.
interfaces.authority: Checkpoint/task/interrupt event content identifies the paused graph state. Current RunRecord status alone does not: a graph that returns normally at an interrupt is recorded as success unless explicitly cancelled.
interfaces.durability: Interrupt and task state follow checkpointer durability. Run status persists separately and may say success for a normal interrupt return.
interfaces.security_boundary: Path run/thread lookup is owner-checked, while the documented body.config thread-namespace seam still applies to execution config.
interfaces.notes: This generic LangGraph mechanism is distinct from ask_clarification, which ends the turn rather than pausing it.

interfaces.producer: LangGraph astream namespaces and worker lifecycle
interfaces.input: messages-tuple deltas/tool messages, updates, custom events, interrupts, metadata, usage, errors, and end signals.
interfaces.transport: In-memory bounded append-only event log with monotonic event IDs and subscriber condition signaling.
interfaces.receiver: Gateway SSE consumers and run event persistence hooks.
interfaces.output: Ordered StreamEvent records; Last-Event-ID replay window; heartbeat when idle.
interfaces.authority: Run worker/event bridge order and event IDs are authoritative for live stream sequencing, not for full durable transcript unless the configured event store records it.
interfaces.durability: In-memory bridge retains a bounded 256-event window and is process-local; configured run event backend supplies durability separately.
interfaces.security_boundary: Subscribers are attached through owner-validated run endpoints; bounded retention limits memory amplification.
interfaces.notes: Late subscribers can replay only what remains in the live bounded bridge unless they query durable stores/state.

interfaces.input: Run event subscription with optional Last-Event-ID and disconnect policy.
interfaces.transport: HTTP Server-Sent Events, unbuffered through nginx.
interfaces.receiver: Frontend stream hook or API client parser.
interfaces.output: Incremental assistant text/reasoning, tool calls/results, state/custom/interrupt/error/end events.
interfaces.authority: SSE is a live presentation channel; final run status/checkpoint/artifacts are authoritative after completion.
interfaces.durability: Client event state is transient; event store/checkpoint may persist underlying data.
interfaces.security_boundary: Run ownership is checked before attach; disconnect policy can continue or cancel a run.
interfaces.notes: drf2's deterministic driver deliberately polls RunRecord status instead of parsing SSE.

interfaces.input: Path thread ID plus an existing run ID for get, join, stream join, or cancel; cancellation may include wait and action options.
interfaces.transport: GET run/list/join/stream endpoints and POST cancel or stream-with-action endpoints.
interfaces.receiver: RunManager/live task and run store.
interfaces.output: Run record/list, awaited terminal record, live/replayed SSE when a bridge exists, cancellation result, or conflict/not-found.
interfaces.authority: The live in-memory run record/task is authoritative for immediate execution, streaming, and cancellation. A configured durable store can remain authoritative for stored status after restart; a store-only run has no live stream/task.
interfaces.durability: Stored status survives restart only with a durable run store; MemoryRunStore is process-local. Join/subscription connections and live event bridges are transient.
interfaces.security_boundary: Path-thread ownership and record thread association are checked before control. Those checks do not repair a creation-time effective checkpoint namespace selected through body.config.
interfaces.notes: POST /runs/wait is not an existing-run wait operation; it creates a new run and is itemized separately. With a configured durable store, a hydrated store-only terminal run remains status-readable even when no live event bridge exists.

interfaces.input: Thread-scoped AgentState updates, messages, titles, summaries, interrupts, and checkpoint metadata.
interfaces.transport: LangGraph checkpointer backend selected by harness/gateway or embedded client.
interfaces.receiver: Checkpoint storage.
interfaces.output: Latest/history checkpoint state used by subsequent turns, resume, get_state, and history APIs.
interfaces.authority: Checkpoint is canonical for agent conversational/graph state; sidecar progress/report files are separate artifacts.
interfaces.durability: Depends on configured backend; gateway defaults/config can provide durable DB-backed checkpoints, embedded clients may use their configured/local checkpointer.
interfaces.security_boundary: Checkpoint keys come from the effective RunnableConfig. The gateway path thread is owner-checked and authenticated user_id is server-stamped, but body.config.configurable.thread_id can currently override the no-context branch's path-derived thread namespace.
interfaces.notes: A separate Stage-1 research_checkpoint.json is only a bridge skip plan; it is not itself the LangGraph checkpoint.

interfaces.input: Thread records, run records/status transitions, run events/traces, token usage, timestamps, errors, and selected metadata.
interfaces.transport: Configured store implementations created as gateway singletons.
interfaces.receiver: MemoryRunStore or configured durable database run repository, plus separately configured thread and event stores.
interfaces.output: Queryable thread/run/event history; restart hydration only for record types backed by durable stores.
interfaces.authority: Each store is canonical for its record type; checkpoint and workspace remain separate authorities for graph state and artifacts.
interfaces.durability: Conditional by store. Without a database session factory, the gateway selects MemoryRunStore and run records are lost on restart; thread, checkpoint, and event persistence are independently configured. drf2 config intends SQLite database and JSONL run events.
interfaces.security_boundary: Store access is internal; services enforce user/thread ownership before reads/writes returned to clients.
interfaces.notes: The presence of a store interface does not imply durable deployment. Event retention/truncation settings mean persisted events are an audit channel, not necessarily an unlimited verbatim transcript.

interfaces.producer: Agent/file/tool execution in the thread workspace
interfaces.input: Artifact path/reference scoped to user/thread workspace.
interfaces.transport: Gateway artifact route and file response/metadata APIs.
interfaces.receiver: Browser/API client or deterministic driver reading a host-mapped workspace path.
interfaces.output: Artifact bytes, directory/listing metadata, or not-found/forbidden response.
interfaces.authority: Workspace file bytes are authoritative artifacts; chat text describing a file is not a substitute.
interfaces.durability: Workspace/provider dependent and normally persistent across run completion.
interfaces.security_boundary: User/thread ownership, normalized path containment, file existence/type, and response content-type protections.
interfaces.notes: The drf2 driver can bypass HTTP artifact download only when workspace_root provides a trusted host mapping.

interfaces.input: Thread ID, requested count n, and optional model selection.
interfaces.transport: POST /api/threads/{thread_id}/suggestions.
interfaces.receiver: Suggestion router/model, then HTTP client.
interfaces.output: Cleaned follow-up question list or empty list.
interfaces.authority: Suggestions are optional UI assistance, not conversation state or pipeline instructions.
interfaces.durability: Not persisted into thread state by the endpoint.
interfaces.security_boundary: Thread ownership and global feature flag; only bounded recent messages are sent to the suggestion model.

passes_and_receptions.payload: bounded recent conversation and JSON-list instruction

interfaces.notes: Current embedded Stage-1 never calls this API; drf2 disables it.

interfaces.input: prompt, mode (full or research_only), project_name, depth, optional max_rounds, language or its accepted research_language alias, and model.
interfaces.transport: POST /api/research/run JSON; SDK alias delegates to the same orchestrator.
interfaces.receiver: Flask research route -> preflight -> PipelineOrchestrator.start.
interfaces.output: Immediate pipeline_id, task_id, mode, and initial status, or validation/preflight errors.
interfaces.authority: Pipeline state created by PipelineOrchestrator is authoritative; request values are validated before launch.
interfaces.durability: pipeline_state.json persists the accepted request/options and lifecycle.
